objective: Implement the platform-independent C safety state machine for the MCU, with deterministic fail-closed transitions and the same transition suite running on Host and QEMU.
acceptance: The C core exposes IDLE, EXECUTING, SAFE_STOP and FAULT states with deterministic results.
STOP is processed from every state, is idempotent, and never permits motion to continue.
WATCHDOG_EXPIRED enters a latched FAULT state with the frozen watchdog fault meaning.
SAFE_STOP and FAULT cannot resume execution through ordinary events or an unauthorized reset.
A trusted reset requires an explicit authorization and cleared-cause gate, then enters IDLE only.
Invalid events and invalid event arguments return a rejection and fail closed without heap allocation.
The core includes no vendor or platform headers, dynamic allocation, floating point, or hardware register access.
The shared transition tests cover every state and event boundary and run against the same core source on Host and QEMU.
The C core and shared C transition suite are authoritative; firmware/virtual_mcu is retired as a safety reference and parity oracle, remaining only as a legacy compatibility stub.
evidence: Host transition-suite output with assertion and failure counts
QEMU transition-suite output from the shared C test source
verify-no-fp output proving no floating-point instructions or allocator symbols
repository test, contract, scenario and context-check output
stop_conditions: The implementation requires changing the frozen JSON Schema, Pydantic models or protocol documentation.
A reset opcode or reset frame would be added to protocol v1.0.
The implementation needs CAN layout, frame decoding, retry deduplication or watchdog timer scheduling from #54, #61 or #60.
The implementation needs vendor headers, board registers, motor control, PID or physical hardware claims.
The C state machine cannot run unchanged in both Host and QEMU targets.
The Python VirtualMcu would need behavior changes or a parity claim outside this Task Packet; handle that separately, especially unknown-command handling from #63.
